---
title: "Setup check: Python and R in one notebook"
format: html
---

This notebook checks that Python (uv) and R (renv) both work. Because it has an
R chunk, Quarto renders it with **knitr**, and the Python chunks run through
**reticulate** using the project's `.venv`. Objects pass between languages:
`py$name` in R, `r.name` in Python.

## Simulate in Python

```{python}
from stpp import simulate_poisson

events = simulate_poisson(rate=200, T=1.0, seed=42)
print(f"{len(events)} events")
```

## Analyse in R

```{r}
ev <- as.data.frame(py$events)
names(ev) <- c("t", "x", "y")
summary(ev)
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Simulated homogeneous Poisson events, coloured by time"
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(ev, aes(x, y, colour = t)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Back to Python

```{python}
n_r = r.ev.shape[0]
assert n_r == len(events)
print("Round trip OK")
```
